tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint Type for Scale Models
tips.text: For acrylic paints, Vallejo Model Color (Item 73022) is ideal for dry-brushing and washes due to its high pigment load. Enamel paints like Tamiya Acrylic Enamel (Item 87004) offer harder finishes and better adhesion to plastic, suitable for final gloss coats. Lacquer paints (AMMO by Mig Jimenez, Item 4353) are fast-drying and provide a very hard, glass-like finish, perfect for metallics. Always thin enamel and lacquer with Tami, 10-20% water for acrylics. Test on a small area first to avoid color shifts or cracking.

tips.title: Optimal Sandpaper Grits for Model Detailing
tips.text: Start with 400-grit sandpaper (Tamiya 87006) for coarse scratches on plastic parts, then 1000-grit (Tamiya 87007) for fine smoothing. For the final stages, use 2000-grit (Tamiya 87008) to eliminate all surface imperfections. Always sand in a well-ventilated area with a sanding block or sponge. Wipe with a damp cloth after each grit to remove dust and debris. Avoid using 600-grit for final polishing as it leaves a hazy surface.

tips.title: Choosing the Best Filler for Plastic Gaps
tips.text: Tamiya Putty (Item 87009) is perfect for filling small gaps in polystyrene models, while Vallejo Plastic Putty (Item 73055) works better on ABS plastics. For a faster alternative, mix super glue with baking soda (3:1 ratio) to create a quick-setting filler. Apply with a fine brush, press into the gap, and let dry for 10 minutes. Sand with 1000-grit paper afterward. Avoid using epoxy putty for small gaps as it's too rigid and hard to sand.

tips.title: Selecting Photo-Etch vs Resin Details
tips.text: Photo-etch (PE) parts from ICM (Item 3001) and Eduard (Item 1001) are thinner, more detailed, and ideal for intricate components like gun sights and aircraft panels. Resin parts from Clear Prop Models (Item 9901) are thicker, more durable, and better suited for large-scale or rough handling. PE requires careful bending with a PE bender, while resin parts can be sanded with 600-grit paper. Always clean PE parts with isopropyl alcohol before assembly to remove mold release agents.

tips.title: Using the Right Decal Setting Solutions
tips.text: Micro Set (Item 7310) is the best for setting decals on acrylic paints due to its clear, strong bond. Mr. Mark Softer (Item 7308) is ideal for enamel or lacquer finishes as it dissolves the decal’s adhesive slowly, reducing bubbling. For lacquer decals, use Clear Prop Models’ Microscale Solution (Item 7309) which is specifically formulated for fast-drying lacquers. Apply a thin layer with a brush, press the decal firmly, and allow 24 hours to cure. Test on a small area first to avoid decal distortion.
